record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Find a simple usable approximation scheme that accurately determines the gravitational radiation produced by an isolated astrophysical system, and in particular prove the quadrupole radiation formula.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an isolated astrophysical system modeled as a solution of the Einstein vacuum (or Einstein–matter) field equations
\[ R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac12 R\, g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}, \]
on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold which is asymptotically flat at spatial and null infinity, with compactly supported (or sufficiently localized) stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ describing the matter source.

Develop a simple, usable approximation scheme (for example, a controlled post-Newtonian or post-Minkowskian expansion together with a near-zone/far-zone matching) that accurately determines the gravitational radiation emitted to null infinity by such an isolated source. In particular, give a mathematically rigorous derivation, within general relativity (not merely linearized theory), of the quadrupole radiation formula
\[ \frac{dE}{dt} \;=\; -\frac{G}{5c^{5}}\,\Big\langle \dddot{Q}_{ij}\,\dddot{Q}^{ij}\Big\rangle, \]
where
\[ Q_{ij}(t) \;=\; \int \rho(t,\mathbf{x})\Big(x_i x_j - \tfrac{1}{3}\delta_{ij}|\mathbf{x}|^{2}\Big)\,d^{3}x \]
is the trace-free mass quadrupole moment of the source, $\rho$ is its mass-energy density, and $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denotes a suitable time average. The derivation must:
(i) start from the full nonlinear Einstein equations,
(ii) yield error estimates controlled by an explicit small parameter (e.g. the ratio of source velocity to the speed of light, or the ratio of Schwarzschild radius to source size), and
(iii) justify the formula as an asymptotic statement about energy flux through future null infinity.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Blanchet and Damour developed a multipolar post-Minkowskian formalism that systematically expands the vacuum Einstein equations exterior to the source and matches it to a post-Newtonian near-zone expansion, leading to a derivation of the quadrupole formula and its higher-order corrections. Damour also provided derivations valid in the Newtonian limit. These results are widely accepted within the post-Newtonian framework and are central to gravitational-wave template construction, but a fully rigorous mathematical proof from the nonlinear Einstein equations with controlled error bounds (in the sense of mathematical relativity) remains incomplete. Hence the broader problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The quadrupole radiation formula
status_evidence.snippet: Damour's article addressing the derivation of the quadrupole radiation formula within general relativity.
status_evidence.claim: There is published work explicitly aimed at proving the quadrupole formula in GR.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational Radiation from Post-Newtonian Sources and Inspiralling Compact Binaries (Blanchet)
status_evidence.snippet: Blanchet–Damour multipolar post-Minkowskian formalism iterates the vacuum field equations and yields radiative multipole moments as functionals of source moments, providing the quadrupole formula and its corrections.
status_evidence.claim: A systematic approximation scheme exists and reproduces the quadrupole formula to leading order with controlled higher-order extensions.

status_evidence.title: Gravitational radiation and the validity of the far-zone quadrupole formula in the Newtonian limit of general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes validity of the far-zone quadrupole formula in the Newtonian limit of general relativity.
status_evidence.claim: Validity of the quadrupole formula has been established rigorously in a Newtonian-limit regime.
